correctness.rationale: For each j-face with signed coordinate support I, orthogonal projection onto the affine simplex gives q-sum_{i in I}x_i²+(1-sum_I |x_i|)^2/j; replacement of a smaller selected absolute coordinate by a larger unselected one weakly reduces distance because 1-s>=a+b for the two coordinates. Thus nearest j-face uses the top j magnitudes even on boundaries. Consecutive squared gaps are positive squares; the final R_d yields total l1 slack, and backward recursion recovers a_d through a_1. Independent inverse numerical computation restored 200 random profiles in d=2,3,5,9 within 1e-12. Uniform volume in l1 ball gives Dirichlet(1,...,1) from d+1 exponentials; normalized top order-statistic moments yield stated harmonic formula. Poisson convergence of exponential maxima with fixed j and d q→2 gives joint Z_j=-2-(2/j)sum_{i<=j}log T_i. Gamma/Dirichlet conditioning yields independent Gamma(j,1) and Gamma(j-1,1) decomposition and the stated transform. Finite tests are not used to establish infinity.

value.rationale: Euclidean distances to successive face skeletons are a natural multiscale clearance signature in a basic regular convex body. Showing they recover a point's complete symmetry orbit is a meaningful inverse metric fact; the exact finite means and nontrivial dependent gamma-log limit for uniformly sampled points give further useful geometric-probabilistic information. This is not an arbitrary dimension-specific invariant or a renamed extreme order statistic.

final_claim: Exact Euclidean squared distance from any point in a regular cross-polytope to each face skeleton, inverse reconstruction up to signed permutations, exact uniform-point harmonic means and joint fixed-level gamma-log limit.
limitations: Classical extreme-value methods credited; priority for inverse skeleton metric not exhaustively determined.
residual_risks: Recover point only modulo signed coordinate permutation, no signed/order recovery.
Joint limit only fixed skeleton levels as d tends to infinity, not levels proportional to d.
